messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache metadata growth spike detected in paged-kv (svc=runtime-pool-2). metadata_count ↑ 4.7x, eviction-rate ↑ 3x, client errors starting around 03:12 UTC. Auto-escalation to #eng-sre. Pager sent to @mike_sre and @julia_runtime :rotating_light:

mike_sre: I'm on it. Seeing continuous-batching throughput double over last 10m, lots of prefetch requests. Initial hypothesis: prefetch storm + large block size causing metadata explosion and eviction thrash.

julia_runtime: Confirmed. Metrics: blocked pages in memstore increased, blockmgr queue length spiked and CPU on blockmgr hosts saturated. Some downstream embed endpoints returning 502s due to cache lookup timeouts.

anna_prod: Customer impact: a handful of high-volume tenants reporting latency > 3s on text-generation calls, some request timeouts. CS notified.

sam_ops: Dumping a quick view of recent logs for the block manager:
```
[2024-08-02T03:12:05Z] blockmgr[worker-7]: prefetch request id=abc123 size=8MB keyset=kv_range_42
[2024-08-02T03:12:06Z] blockmgr[worker-7]: allocate block 8MB -> success
[2024-08-02T03:12:07Z] blockmgr[worker-7]: metadata write latency=430ms
[2024-08-02T03:12:08Z] blockmgr[worker-7]: eviction scan started, evicting 6 blocks
[2024-08-02T03:12:10Z] blockmgr[worker-7]: error=metadata-store-throttle
```

mike_sre: OK let's do short mitigations: 1) disable speculative prefetch globally on runtime-pool-2, 2) set continuous-batching max window to 16ms (was 64ms), 3) temporarily reduce block size to 2MB for new allocations. Planning to push hotfix to feature-flag config. Anyone object?

julia_runtime: +1. Also add a temporary throttle on prefetch concurrency: MAX_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=8. That should stop the thundering prefetch.

chen_eng: I'll prepare the rollout. Hotfix commands (deploy via infra-ops):
```bash
# set FF to disable speculative prefetch
redwoodctl config set runtime-pool-2.experimental.speculative_prefetch false --env=prod --ff
# reduce batch window
redwoodctl config set runtime-pool-2.continuous_batch.window_ms 16 --env=prod --ff
# cap prefetch concurrency
redwoodctl config set runtime-pool-2.prefetch.max_concurrency 8 --env=prod --ff
# set block allocation size for new blocks
redwoodctl config set blockmgr.default_block_size_bytes 2097152 --env=prod --ff
```

sam_ops: I'll kick the config change and watch rollout. Doing staged apply to zone-a then zone-b.

natalie_pm: Noting customer comms: we'll tell impacted tenants we've throttled aggressive prefetching and are monitoring; ETA for full recovery TBD.

incident-bot: ACTION: created incident-1732109876 in incident tracker, severity=P2, runbook=https://intra.redwood/ops/runbooks/paged-kv.md

mike_sre: Rolling now to zone-a. Watch metrics: metadata_count, eviction_rate, blockmgr_cpu, 5xx_rate on generation endpoints. If 5xx doesn't drop in 5m, consider rollback of latest runtime change.

(5m later)

sam_ops: zone-a changes applied. Metrics: metadata_count down 62%, eviction-rate down 55%, 5xx down to baseline-ish, p50 latency decreased ~420ms. No new errors in logs aside from transient throttle messages.

julia_runtime: Good. Proceeding to zone-b. We'll keep speculative prefetch disabled for 2h and then experiment with smaller increments. Need a postmortem to tune default block size and eviction policy under heavy prefetch.

anna_prod: Customer updates sent. CS reports two tenants saw degraded experience but no data loss, they accepted the mitigation.

natalie_pm: Scheduling follow-up: retrospective + quota analysis + stress test suite for prefetch bursts. Assigning action items:
- mike_sre: write postmortem draft (due +48h)
- chen_eng: add e2e test that simulates concurrent prefetches and validates metadata growth (due +72h)
- julia_runtime: propose new default block size & eviction heuristics (due +72h)

mike_sre: Leaving a note for oncall handoff to eveningshift: incident is contained, metrics stable. Handoff to @julia_runtime in 30m.

julia_runtime: Taking follow-up oncall. Adding extra alert: metadata_count > 1.5x baseline for >2m -> page eng-sre.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, customer impact limited, monitoring continued. Severity downgraded to P3.

chen_eng: I'll open a more detailed engineering task for blockmgr: consider adaptive block sizing, add backpressure early in prefetch path, and improve logging for metadata ops.

mike_sre: Thanks all. Final note: don't forget to annotate the deploy that preceded this with the config flags that hit canary — we need the correlation in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
